reasoning: Recent polling and coverage over the last month and a half show an extremely tight but slightly Democratic-tilting Alaska Senate race, while there is no fresh, state-specific general-election presidential polling in that window. The clearest quantified signal is the early‑August Alaska Survey Research poll and the August Data for Progress survey, both showing Mary Peltola narrowly ahead of Dan Sullivan, balanced against a late‑June/early‑July New York Times/Siena poll that had Sullivan up by 2 and at least one right‑leaning aggregation arguing Sullivan by several points; taken together, they suggest a true race margin hovering around even but currently best described as roughly D+1 in the Senate contest, with the state’s structural lean still R+6 by Cook PVI. Given the lack of new presidential polling in the last 45 days, no current, data‑grounded partisan margin can be assigned to the presidential race beyond that structural R+ tilt.

sources.name: Data for Progress
sources.details: Data for Progress poll of 605 likely Alaska voters found Mary Peltola leading Sen. Dan Sullivan in the 2026 Senate race, described as Peltola in the lead in an affordability-focused survey memo (exact horse‑race margin characterized as a narrow edge).

sources.name: Alaska Survey Research (reported by Newsweek)
sources.details: Alaska Survey Research general-election poll of 1,371 likely voters found Peltola 50.8% and Sullivan 49.2% in the final ranked-choice round for the 2026 U.S. Senate race, a D+1.6 lead within the margin of error.

sources.name: USA Today (summarizing Alaska Survey Research and NYT/Siena)
sources.details: USA Today article summarizing Alaska Survey Research reports Peltola holding a 1.6‑point edge over Sullivan in an August poll, while also noting earlier surveys with Sullivan +2 and Peltola +7, framing the race as highly competitive with Peltola currently ahead.

sources.name: New York Times/Siena College (via Washington Examiner/Newsweek coverage)
sources.details: New York Times/Siena College poll cited in multiple stories found Dan Sullivan leading Mary Peltola 47%-45% in the 2026 Alaska Senate race’s initial ranked-choice round, a 2‑point Republican edge within the margin of error.

sources.name: Alaska Survey Research (earlier 2026 polls, via Washington Examiner)
sources.details: Washington Examiner article recounts earlier Alaska Survey Research polls showing Peltola leading Sullivan 49%-44% in March and 49%-43% in April, characterizing the contest as one of 2026’s most closely watched with mixed but often Peltola-leaning results.

sources.name: Pollsmax model (reported by RedState)
sources.details: RedState article describing Pollsmax aggregation claims its model projects Sullivan to win the Alaska Senate race over Peltola by 5.8 points and forecasts overall GOP dominance in Alaska’s 2026 contests.

sources.name: Siena University (via Washington Examiner)
sources.details: Washington Examiner notes a Siena University poll from early July showing Sullivan 47% to Peltola 45% in the Alaska Senate race, reinforcing the picture of a narrow Republican edge in that specific survey but an overall toss-up environment.

sources.name: Cook Political Report rating (as reported by Washington Examiner)
sources.details: Washington Examiner coverage describes the Alaska Senate race as one of the most closely watched of 2026, citing polls that collectively show a tight contest and noting that the Cook Political Report rates the race as a toss-up.

sources.name: USA Today (narrative framing of Alaska Senate race)
sources.details: USA Today profile states that Democrat Mary Peltola is leading polls in reliably red Alaska, emphasizing her narrow polling advantages over Sullivan and national Democrats’ hopes of flipping the seat.

sources.name: Newsweek (narrative framing of Alaska Senate race)
sources.details: Newsweek article reports that Dan Sullivan is within striking distance of Mary Peltola, framing the Alaska Senate race as a crucial battleground with Peltola narrowly ahead in the latest poll and Sullivan leading in another, underscoring the toss-up nature of the contest.

sources.name: ABC News (primary results context)
sources.details: ABC News live primary results page notes that Republican Sen. Dan Sullivan and former Democratic congresswoman Mary Peltola advanced to the general election in Alaska’s 2026 Senate race, without indicating a general-election favorite.

sources.name: Cook Political Report PVI (via Wikipedia summary)
sources.details: Cook Political Report’s PVI map and Wikipedia summary list Alaska’s statewide Cook Partisan Voting Index as R+6, indicating the state voted about six points more Republican than the nation in recent presidential elections.
sources.date_range: As of latest Cook PVI update referenced July 29, 2026
